units_unreached.why: Remote-client-only. Every caller (imaging capture_panel, calibration_section, flat-wizard save_path_dialog, onboarding capture_dir_step) branches on isRemote and falls back to file_selector's getDirectoryPath when the app is driving local hardware. Confirmed live: Imaging > File Settings > Save Path folder button opened the native GTK 'Choose Directory' chooser (accessibility tree showed 'file chooser: Choose Directory'), not this dialog. Reaching it needs a paired remote/headless host, which this sandbox has no backend for.

Same isRemote gate — plate_solving_settings_screen, calibration_settings and phd2_guiding_settings all call it only when isRemote is true, otherwise they use the native open/save-file dialogs. Not reachable from a local desktop session.

Instantiated only by apps/mobile (screens/dashboard/tabs/devices_tab.dart:101). Zero instantiations anywhere in the desktop app — the desktop Guiding screen renders its own Guide Graph/RMS readouts instead. Not reachable from the surface under audit.

Startup-only surface with exactly one call site (screens/shell/app_shell.dart:310) and it never fires on this machine. The gate needs BOTH star and DSO catalogs to be missing, but CatalogManager stores them in the SHARED application-support directory, not in SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/catalogs/ already holds hyg_v42.csv, NGC.csv, glade_plus_galaxies.csv, dso_metadata.json, deep_stars/ etc. So starStatus.isInstalled && dsoStatus.isInstalled are true for every sandbox profile and the dialog is suppressed. Wiping the developer's real catalog directory is the only way to reach it, which is not acceptable in a sweep. Verified the other two gates were satisfied: an equipment profile exists (so shouldRunEquipmentOnboarding is false) and app_settings has no 'catalog_setup_skipped' row.

Renders only when backendProvider is a NetworkBackend (remote/paired client) and its websocket is inside the reconnect grace window; _handleRetry itself bails with 'The remote session is no longer available' when the backend is not a NetworkBackend. The audited instance is a local desktop host with no paired remote, so the banner never mounts. Reaching it needs a second machine or a headless host to pair with.

Mounted at the app root (app.dart:198) but only surfaces when the database open fails and a recovery/backup path exists. This run RESUMED an earlier attempt: the first 7 units, 6 verified-correct entries and findings 1-5 are that attempt's work and were kept verbatim; everything from widget:weather_status_card.dart onward is new. Method: driven on display :88 with profile r-shared-widgets against the prebuilt Linux release bundle. Startup-gated dialogs (session recovery, quick start, night story) were reached by seeding the scratch sqlite DB directly and relaunching - note that Drift stores these DateTime columns as unix SECONDS, and my first seed used milliseconds, which made the recovery dialog render '58555-11-05'; that was my bad data, not a defect, and it is not reported. Every claim about a number was checked against the DB or against an external ground truth (Open-Meteo and the actual RainViewer tile for the weather card).

Two would-be findings were killed by that checking and are recorded as verified-correct instead: the weather card's alarming 'Cloud Cover 100% Overcast / Critical' is TRUE (Open-Meteo returns cloud_cover:100 for the observer lat/lon, even though the radar tile there is fully transparent), and 'Discard All' on the session-recovery dialog looked like a silent no-op until I noticed it had opened a nested confirmation.

findings.title: Readiness panel reports a green "Profile devices — every device is connected" over an empty profile with nothing connected
findings.what_happened: On a fresh profile (My Equipment, 0 devices) with camera/mount/guider all disconnected, the readiness panel shows a GREEN dot on 'Profile devices' with the text 'Every device assigned in the active profile is connected.' The status bar in the same frame reads 'Camera Disconnected  Mount Disconnected  Guider Disconnected'.
findings.expected: With zero devices assigned the row should read 'No devices assigned to this profile' in a neutral/warn state, not a green all-connected pass. A vacuous truth over an empty set is the single most misleading thing a readiness panel can say.
findings.repro: Fresh profile -> Equipment -> 'I'll do it manually' -> right STATUS rail -> 'View all (3 more)' -> read the 'Profile devices' row while the status bar shows every device disconnected.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-09.png (dialog row 'Profile devices' green + 'Every device assigned in the active profile is connected.'; status bar bottom: Camera Disconnected / Mount Disconnected / Guider Disconnected; profile card reads '0 devices')
findings.proposed_fix: Special-case the empty-assignment case in the profile-devices readiness check: emit a distinct 'no devices assigned' item (warn) instead of the all-connected pass.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live on the rebuilt bundle: profile 'My Equipment' showing '0 devices' / 'No devices assigned', status bar reading Camera Disconnected / Mount Disconnected / Guider Disconnected, and the full readiness dialog rendering 'Profile devices — Every device assigned in the active profile is connected.' Source is unambiguous: _buildProfileDevices returns ReadinessLevel.ready (green) whenever offlineProfileDevices.isEmpty, with no branch for 'the profile assigns nothing at all'. Severity downgraded P2->P3: in the same panel 'Critical devices' correctly blocks on the disconnected camera and the summary correctly reads 'Not ready / 2 items are blocking first light', so the panel as a whole never claims the rig is ready.
findings.location_wrong: Yes. The claim points at packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/readiness/readiness_panel.dart, which only renders items it is handed. The text, the level, and the missing empty-profile branch are all in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/readiness/readiness_models.dart:369-392 (input computed at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/readiness_provider.dart:105-112).

findings.title: Dismissing a blocking readiness item hides it while the summary keeps counting it, so the panel claims 3 blockers and lists 2
findings.what_happened: Clicking the X on the blocking 'Critical devices' row (camera not connected) removes the row from the rail, but the summary line above it still reads '3 items are blocking first light.' while only 2 blocking rows remain visible and the hidden one is only reachable via a small 'Show 1 dismissed' link.
findings.expected: Either blocking items should not be dismissable at all (NINA/SGP do not let you hide a hard blocker), or the summary must say '3 blocking (1 hidden)' so the count and the list agree.
findings.repro: Equipment -> right STATUS rail -> click the X on 'Critical devices' -> read the summary line vs the rows shown.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-10.png — summary '3 items are blocking first light.' above only 'Observing location' and 'Capture output folder' blockers plus an amber 'Plate solver'; 'Show 1 dismissed' at the bottom restores it correctly.
findings.proposed_fix: Exclude dismissed items from the blocking count, or annotate the count with the hidden total.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Equipment > STATUS rail read 'Ready to image / 2 items are blocking first light.' over Critical devices (red), Capture output folder (red), Plate solver (amber). Clicked the X on 'Critical devices'; the row vanished, 'Show 1 dismissed' appeared, and the summary STILL read '2 items are blocking first light.' with exactly one blocking row visible (screenshot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sw-10.png). Exact numbers differ from the claim (2/1 not 3/2) only because I had set an observing location, clearing one blocker; the mismatch is identical.
findings.location_wrong: Partially. The lying count string is packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/equipment/widgets/equipment_readiness_panel.dart:68-71 (_subtitle), NOT readiness_panel.dart — this usage passes showHeader:false so readiness_panel.dart's own _summaryDetail (:254-274) never renders. readiness_panel.dart:168-173 (the dismissal filter) is the other half, so the cited file alone is only half the fix.

findings.title: Shell equipment indicator reads "0/0 — No devices configured" while four devices are connected
findings.what_happened: After connecting Simulated Camera, Mount, Focuser and Filter Wheel from Equipment > Discovery, the always-visible status-bar equipment chip still reads '🔭 My Equipment ● 0/0' and its popup body says 'No devices configured'. In the same frame the Equipment header says '4 connected · 4 unsaved', all four device rows say Connected, and the status pills read 'Camera Simulated Camera', 'Mount Simulated Mount', 'Focus 25000'. The count is derived from devices ASSIGNED to the profile, not from what is connected, so any session-only connection (the exact flow the app itself offers with 'This session only — not saved to your profile') is invisible to the shell indicator.
findings.expected: The chip should count live connections, e.g. '4 connected' or '4/0 assigned', and its menu should list the connected devices with a Disconnect for each. Saying 'No devices configured' while four devices are streaming is the shell telling the operator the rig is empty.
findings.repro: Equipment -> 'I'll do it manually' -> Discovery Expand -> Connect on Simulated Camera, Mount, Focuser, Filter Wheel -> click the '🔭 My Equipment 0/0' chip at the far left of the status bar.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-17-status-0of0-with-4-connected.png — popup 'My Equipment ● 0/0' + 'No devices configured' next to header '4 connected · 4 unsaved' and four green Connected rows.
findings.proposed_fix: Count connected devices from the device state providers regardless of profile membership; show 'connected/assigned' only when an assignment exists, otherwise 'N connected (session only)'.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Session-connected Simulated Camera, Mount, Focuser and Filter Wheel from Equipment > Discovery. Same frame: header '4 connected · 4 unsaved', four Connected device rows, status-bar pills 'Camera / Simulated Camera', 'Mount / Simulated Mount', 'Focus / 25000' — and the shell chip 'My Equipment 0/0'. Clicking the chip gives a popup whose entire body is 'No devices configured' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sw-23.png). Source: _countConnectedDevices (:91-112) requires profileDeviceId != null so a session-only connection can never be counted, and the guard at :167 (!hasAnyDevice && connectedCount == 0) then suppresses every per-device row in favour of the 'No devices configured' literal at :173. Location cited (_countConnectedDevices / _countDevicesInProfile) is exact.

findings.title: 'Disconnect All' stays enabled and silently no-ops when nothing is connected
findings.what_happened: With 0 devices connected the equipment-status popup still offers a fully enabled 'Disconnect All' item. Clicking it closes the menu and does nothing — no toast, no log line, no state change.
findings.expected: Disable (grey) 'Disconnect All' when connectedCount == 0, like every other dead action in this build is greyed.
findings.repro: Fresh profile, nothing connected -> click the equipment chip in the status bar -> 'Disconnect All'. Watch the tree and drive_linux.py log: no change, no message.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-12.png shows 'No devices configured' above a normal-weight (enabled) 'Disconnect All'; the accessibility tree reports 'button: Disconnect All' with no [DISABLED] state; app log shows no entry after the click.
findings.proposed_fix: Gate the Disconnect All PopupMenuItem's enabled flag on connectedCount > 0.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Source is decisive: the 'Disconnect All' PopupMenuItem at equipment_status_indicator.dart:325-343 takes no `enabled:` argument at all, so it is unconditionally enabled regardless of connectedCount, and _disconnectAll (:453-468) only surfaces a message for summary.failures. Live: with all four devices disconnected, the popup showed greyed-italic 'No devices configured' above a normal-weight 'Disconnect All'; clicking it closed the menu, the app log stayed at exactly 155 lines before and after, no toast, no state change. CAVEAT on the claim's stated evidence: 'the tree reports button: Disconnect All with no [DISABLED] state' is NOT probative — the sibling 'No devices configured' item has enabled:false in source and also reports without DISABLED, because a disabled PopupMenuItem is not focusable and drive_linux.py:387-389 only emits DISABLED for focusable/selectable/checkable nodes. Downgraded P3->P4: harmless affordance polish; the popup line directly above already says 'No devices configured'.

findings.title: Guiding-control buttons are invisible to assistive tech: exposed as generic panels with no button role and no disabled state
findings.what_happened: The accessibility tree for the Guiding Controls block reports 'panel: Start', 'panel: Pause', 'panel: Loop Exposures', 'panel: Auto Select', 'panel: Deselect', 'panel: Dither Now' — role 'panel', never 'button', and never [DISABLED] even though all six are logically disabled (onPressed == null) while PHD2 is disconnected. Every other button in the app in the same tree dump reports 'button: <label>' and picks up [DISABLED] correctly (e.g. 'panel: Settle Settings [DISABLED]', 'button: Connect').
findings.expected: These are the controls that start and stop guiding. They should expose a button role and their enabled/disabled state, so a screen-reader user is told 'Start, button, dimmed' rather than a nameless panel.
findings.repro: Guiding screen with PHD2 disconnected -> drive_linux.py tree -> read the Guiding Controls subtree.
findings.evidence: tree output at 14:41 shows 'panel: Start / panel: Pause / panel: Loop Exposures / panel: Star Selection / panel: Auto Select / panel: Deselect / panel: Dither' with no roles or states; the same dump has 'button: Connect' and 'panel: Settle Settings [DISABLED]' so the harness does read roles and states when they are published.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/phd2/guide_controls_panel.dart (_actionButton builds a bare Material+InkWell with no Semantics(button: true, enabled: ...))
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the InkWell in Semantics(button: true, enabled: !isDisabled, label: label) or use the design-system button widget that already publishes those flags.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live with PHD2 disconnected: the Guiding tree returns 'panel: Start', 'panel: Pause', 'panel: Loop Exposures', 'panel: Auto Select', 'panel: Deselect', 'panel: Dither Now' — role panel, never button, never [DISABLED] — in the same dump that carries 'button: Connect', proving the harness reads roles when published. Source confirms: the shared builder is a bare Material > InkWell > ConstrainedBox > AnimatedContainer > Row(Icon, Text) with no Semantics wrapper, and when isDisabled it passes onTap: null so the InkWell publishes no tap semantics either.
findings.location_wrong: Minor. File is right (packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/phd2/guide_controls_panel.dart) but the method is _buildControlButton at :765-850, not '_actionButton'.

findings.title: Weather status card renders an epoch-zero timestamp as 'Updated 20667 days ago' before the first fetch lands
findings.what_happened: On first paint of the Weather screen - before the RainViewer/Open-Meteo fetch returns - the card's footer reads 'Updated 20667 days ago'. 20667 days before 2026-08-02 is 1970-01-01, i.e. lastUpdate is DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(0), not null. Roughly 30 seconds later the same slot reads 'Updated 0 sec ago'.
findings.expected: With no data yet the card should say 'Waiting for data' (or hide the footer). Telling the operator their weather data is 56 years old is worse than saying nothing, and 'Updated 20667 days ago' is not a phrase any user can act on.
findings.repro: Launch fresh, click Weather in the sidebar, run `drive_linux.py tree --profile r-shared-widgets` within the first ~20 seconds while the radar is still loading.
findings.evidence: tree at 10:24 (weather screen, still showing 'No radar frames available'): 'panel: Updated 20667 days ago'. tree at 10:26 in the same slot: 'panel: Updated 0 sec ago'.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat a lastUpdate at or near the epoch as absent: in the weather status provider leave lastUpdate null until the first successful fetch, and have _formatLastUpdate return 'never' for anything older than, say, a day.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on the rebuilt bundle: set Settings > Location to lat -33.9 / lon 74.0, opened Weather, tree reads 'panel: Updated 20668 days ago' — one MORE than the original 20667, exactly as an epoch-0 sentinel predicts now that the date rolled from 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-03. Root cause: weather_providers.dart:582 'lastUpdate: lastFetchedAt ?? DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(0)' with WeatherStatus.lastUpdate non-nullable, so the card's 'if (widget.lastUpdate != null)' at :240 can never be false. Note the state is not transient: with no network it persists for the whole session, not just the first ~20 s.
findings.location_wrong: Partially. Rendering lines are right (weather_status_card.dart:242 Text; _formatLastUpdate is at :125-138, not :120-137) but the fix belongs at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/weather_providers.dart:582 and the non-nullable WeatherStatus.lastUpdate field; a fixer sent only to the card will find a null-guard that is already there.

findings.title: Radar timeline opens on the OLDEST frame, so the Weather screen shows two-hour-stale cloud by default
findings.what_happened: Navigating to Weather leaves the scrubber at 'Frame 1 of 13' / 08:20 with the playhead pinned to the far left, while the wall clock was 10:26 and the scrubber's own green NOW marker sits at the far right over frame 13. The map you are looking at is therefore 2 hours out of date until you press play or drag.
findings.expected: A cloud radar should open on the newest frame (frame 13 / NOW) and let you scrub BACK to see where the cloud came from. That is what RainViewer's own viewer, Clear Outside and the ASIAIR's sky view all do. Opening two hours in the past is the one state that can make you decide to keep imaging under cloud that has already arrived.
findings.repro: Sidebar -> Weather. Read 'Frame N of 13' and the time chip next to the scrubber against the clock in the status bar. Observed on first paint with no interaction.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-31-weather.png - 'Frame 1 of 13', time chip '08:20', NOW marker at the right end of the track, status-bar clock '10:26:21'.
findings.proposed_fix: Initialise the frame index to frames.length - 1 (the NOW frame) instead of 0, and have the skip-next button jump to NOW rather than stepping one frame.

findings.title: Slew dropdown drives the mount 69 degrees BELOW the horizon and reports 'Slew complete'
findings.what_happened: With the observer location at lat -33.9 / lon 74.0, I entered RA 5.59 h / Dec +22.01 deg in Imaging > Mount > GoTo/Sync and picked 'Slew' from the dropdown. The command was accepted without any prompt, the mount moved, the Mount Status panel then read 'Alt -69.14 deg' and the app raised a green toast reading 'Slew complete'.
findings.expected: A target at -69 deg altitude is under the ground. NINA refuses (and SGP warns) on a below-horizon GoTo because on a real German-equatorial rig it drives the OTA into the pier or the tripod leg. The shared slew control should compute the target altitude from the site location before dispatching and either block it or require an explicit 'target is 69 deg below the horizon - slew anyway?' confirmation.
findings.repro: Equipment > Discovery > Connect Simulated Mount. Imaging > Mount tab > Unpark. Scroll to GoTo / Sync, type RA 5.59 and Dec 22.01, click the Slew split-button, choose 'Slew'. Read Alt in Mount Status and the toast.
findings.evidence: tree after the slew: 'panel: Alt' / 'panel: -69.14' with RA '05h 35m 24.0s' and Dec '+22 00' 36.0"'; toast 'panel: Slew complete'. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-43-menu.png shows the menu that was used.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/slew_dropdown_button.dart:209-222 (_handleSlew calls mountService.slewTo with no altitude precondition; only the centering paths run _preflightCentering)
findings.proposed_fix: Add a horizon precondition to _handleSlew (and _handleSlewAndCenter) using the existing observer location + horizon-profile providers: refuse, or confirm, when the computed altitude is below the configured minimum altitude.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Site lat -33.9 / lon 74.0, Simulated Mount connected and unparked, RA 5.59 / Dec 22.01 entered in Imaging > Mount > GoTo/Sync, split-button menu > 'Slew'. No prompt of any kind. Mount Status then read RA 05h 35m 24.0s, Dec +22° 00' 36.0", Alt -23.15°, and the toast read 'Slew complete'. I recomputed the altitude by hand rather than trusting the readout: with LST ~22.6 h, HA = 17.04 h = 255.6°, sin(alt) = sin(22.01)sin(-33.9) + cos(22.01)cos(-33.9)cos(255.6) = -0.209 - 0.191 = -0.400 → alt = -23.6°, matching. The magnitude differs from the claim's -69.14° only because LST differs; the target is under the ground either way. Source: mount_command_service.dart:179-206 validates only coordinate RANGE and then unconditionally returns success('Slew complete').
findings.location_wrong: Minor line drift: _handleSlew is at slew_dropdown_button.dart:212-224, not :209-222. Also note _preflightCentering (:345-376) does not check altitude either, so the centering path is no safer — fixing only there would not close the gap.

findings.title: The Slew split-button is invisible to assistive tech - no node at all in the accessibility tree
findings.what_happened: With valid coordinates entered and the mount unparked, the accessibility tree for the GoTo / Sync card contains 'button: Sync' but no node named 'Slew' at all. The control is a PopupMenuButton whose visual child is wrapped in ExcludeSemantics, and the PopupMenuButton itself supplies no label or tooltip, so the primary GoTo action has no accessible name. The menu items ('button: Slew', 'button: Slew & Center') only appear once the menu is already open - which a screen-reader user has no way to discover.
findings.expected: The button should publish a name and enabled state, e.g. Semantics(button: true, label: 'Slew options') on the PopupMenuButton, so it is announced next to Sync.
findings.repro: Imaging > Mount > GoTo/Sync with RA/Dec filled in and the mount unparked -> `drive_linux.py tree --profile r-shared-widgets | grep -i slew`. Only 'ABORT SLEW' and 'Sync' come back.
findings.evidence: tree at 10:35 lists 'button: Park', 'button: Start Track', 'button: ABORT SLEW', 'button: Three-Point Polar Alignment', 'button: Sync' - no 'Slew'. After clicking the chevron the same grep returns 'button: Slew' and 'button: Slew & Center' (the open menu).
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/slew_dropdown_button.dart:153-181 (ExcludeSemantics around the SkotiqButton child of the PopupMenuButton)
findings.proposed_fix: Give the PopupMenuButton a tooltip/semanticLabel, or replace ExcludeSemantics with a MergeSemantics that keeps the 'Slew' label but suppresses the nested button gesture.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live with valid coordinates (5.59 / 22.01) entered and the mount unparked: the GoTo/Sync subtree returns 'button: Sync' and NO node named Slew anywhere, while a region capture (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sw-16.png) shows the Slew split-button rendered, enabled and blue next to Sync. Clicking the chevron makes 'button: Slew' and 'button: Slew & Center' appear — the open menu only. Source at slew_dropdown_button.dart:154-182 is as described: the visual child is IgnorePointer(ExcludeSemantics(SkotiqButton(label:'Slew'))) and the PopupMenuButton at :113-118 supplies no tooltip or label. TRAP WORTH RECORDING: with the coordinate fields EMPTY the tree DOES show 'button: Slew', because mount_tab.dart:425-430 renders a plain disabled SkotiqButton in that state instead of the dropdown — a verifier who does not fill in RA/Dec first will wrongly refute this.

findings.title: The Slew split-button's primary half does nothing - every slew costs two clicks through a menu
findings.what_happened: The control renders as a classic split button: a filled 'Slew' button with a chevron attached. But the whole visual child is wrapped in IgnorePointer, so clicking the 'Slew' half does not slew - it opens the same dropdown as the chevron. You must then click 'Slew' a second time, in the menu.
findings.expected: A split button's primary half performs the default action; only the chevron opens the alternatives. That is how NINA's 'Slew'/'Slew and center' and SGP's target actions behave. As built, the most common action (plain slew) costs two clicks and a menu traversal, and the affordance actively lies about what the left half does.
findings.repro: Imaging > Mount > GoTo/Sync with valid coordinates and the mount unparked. Click the middle of the 'Slew' label (not the chevron). The dropdown opens instead of the mount moving.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-43-menu.png - clicking the 'Slew' body at image (1094,524) produced the menu shown, and the mount only moved after a second click on the menu's 'Slew' row.
findings.proposed_fix: Split the hit area: the label runs _handleSlewMode(SlewMode.slew) directly, the chevron opens the popup.

findings.title: Connection troubleshooter says it 'couldn't pin down the exact cause' while holding an error that names the exact cause, then gives four irrelevant hardware steps
findings.what_happened: Connecting the 'Built-in Multi-Star Guider' from Equipment > Discovery fails and opens Connection help. The headline reads 'The connection didn't complete - The guide camera connection didn't complete and we couldn't pin down the exact cause.' Expanding Technical details in the SAME dialog shows the driver message: 'Built-in guider requires positive guide focal length and camera pixel size (focal_length_mm=0, pixel_size_x_um=3.76, pixel_size_y_um=3.76)'. That is a fully-specified, first-party configuration error. The four suggested steps are 'Check the guide camera is connected and powered / Reseat the cable, confirm power', 'Make sure no other program is using the guide camera', 'Restart Skotiq and reconnect', 'Read the raw error below'. None of them fixes it, and the built-in guider has no cable and no power - it is a software guider that reuses the imaging camera.
findings.expected: The classifier should match its own bridge's error text and say 'Guide scope focal length is not set. Open Equipment > Edit Profile and enter the guide scope focal length in mm.', with a button that jumps there. Sending the operator to reseat a cable on a device that has no cable, and to restart the app, is worse than no advice: they will do it, it will not work, and they will conclude the app is broken.
findings.repro: Equipment > Discovery > Expand > GUIDERS > Connect on 'Built-in Multi-Star Guider' (with a profile whose guide focal length is 0, i.e. any fresh profile). Read the headline, then expand 'Technical details'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-48-tech.png - headline 'we couldn't pin down the exact cause' directly above the expanded Technical details block quoting focal_length_mm=0. Same string again in the fallback toast after Retry.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/troubleshooter/connection_troubleshooter_dialog.dart (classification/knowledge base) - the native message comes from the built-in guider preflight in the Rust bridge.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a knowledge-base rule matching 'requires positive guide focal length' / 'pixel size' to a Configuration cause with a 'Open equipment profile' action, and stop emitting cable/power steps for driverType native built-in devices.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Equipment > Discovery > GUIDERS > Connect on 'Built-in Multi-Star Guider' opens 'Connection help' with headline 'The connection didn't complete' and body 'The guide camera connection didn't complete and we couldn't pin down the exact cause.' The four steps are verbatim as claimed (reseat the cable / confirm power, close other programs, restart Skotiq, read the raw error). Expanding Technical details in the SAME dialog shows 'Failed to connect built-in guider: Operation failed: Built-in guider requires an active profile with a guide focal length' — a fully-specified first-party configuration error. My run hit the sibling branch of the same Rust preflight rather than the claim's exact focal_length_mm=0 string; the classification outcome is identical because that message matches nothing in _configurationMarkers and falls through to DiagnosticCategory.unknown.
findings.location_wrong: Yes. The classification and knowledge base are NOT in packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/troubleshooter/connection_troubleshooter_dialog.dart (that file only renders). They live in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/troubleshooter/connection_diagnostic.dart — _classify at :279-318, _configurationMarkers at :263-274, _headlineFor at :324-339, and the 'couldn't pin down' sentence at :417.

findings.title: First Light dialog accepts a 999999-second exposure and has no upper bound, contradicting its own copy
findings.what_happened: Settings > Help & Tutorials > 'Capture your first light' > Start. The dialog's own helper text reads 'A few seconds is plenty for a first light - long enough to capture stars, short enough to finish quickly.' I replaced the default 5 with 999999 and pressed 'Start capture'. It was accepted without any warning and the native log recorded 'Starting 999999s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50), bin=1x1' - an 11.6-day exposure. The Imaging screen then showed 'Exposing... 999858.8s remaining'.
findings.expected: The field validates the lower bound (0 is refused) but not the upper. A guided first-light flow should clamp to something sane - 60 s is already generous - or at minimum warn above ~120 s. A single fat-fingered keystroke (5 -> 500) silently commits the camera for eight minutes; an extra zero commits it for days.
findings.repro: Settings > Help & Tutorials > Guided Flows > 'Capture your first light' > Start > select the Exposure length field > Ctrl+A > type 999999 > Start capture. Read /tmp/ns-audit/r-shared-widgets/app.log.
findings.evidence: app.log 2026-08-02T14:45:17Z 'Starting 999999s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50), bin=1x1'; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-53-orphan.png 'Exposing... 999858.8s remaining'.
findings.proposed_fix: Clamp the field to a max (e.g. 120 s) with a helper line naming the limit, matching the dialog's own 'a few seconds' promise.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly on display :89, profile v-widgets, with sim_camera_1 connected. Settings > Help & Tutorials > 'Capture your first light' > Start; selected the Exposure length field, Ctrl+A, typed 999999 (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-12.png shows the field holding 999999 with no error), clicked 'Start capture'. Native log /tmp/ns-audit/v-widgets/app.log line 90: '2026-08-02T16:04:41.808335Z INFO Starting 999999s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50), bin=1x1'. Imaging then read 'Exposing... 999938.8s remaining' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-16-imaging.png) at 16:05:42 -- I recomputed it independently: 999999 - 60.2s elapsed = 999938.8, so the countdown is honest and an 11.57-day exposure really was committed. The cited location is correct: first_light_flow_dialog.dart:240-245 _parseExposure rejects only 'value == null || value <= 0', _start (247-262) adds no other check, and the input formatter at 292-294 (FilteringTextInputFormatter.allow(RegExp(r'[0-9.]'))) imposes no length or magnitude limit. Nothing downstream clamps either: FirstLightOrchestrator.run (first_light_orchestrator.dart:233-240) also only rejects <= 0. SEVERITY CORRECTED P1 -> P2: this is a missing guard-rail, not a defect that fires on its own -- the field is pre-filled with a sane 5 and the app does exactly what it was told. Every bit of the 'costs a night' consequence is borrowed from the second finding (no way to cancel); with a working cancel this is a 5-second annoyance. The cheap upper-bound clamp is still the right fix, but a fixer should not be told this is the P1.

findings.title: Closing the First Light dialog mid-capture orphans the exposure, and there is no cancel inside the dialog
findings.what_happened: While the dialog showed 'Working on it... / Capturing exposure' with an indeterminate bar, it offered NO cancel or abort - only the title-bar X. Clicking the X closed the dialog but did NOT stop the exposure: navigating to Imaging showed 'Exposing... 999858.8s remaining' with the camera locked. The Imaging viewer's 'Abort capture' X was then clicked three times (tooltip 'Abort capture' confirmed showing, button highlighted) over ~90 seconds and the countdown kept running (999828.7 -> 999816.7 -> 999800.7 -> 999766.7); no abort request appears anywhere in the native log. The camera stayed unusable.
findings.expected: Dismissing a modal that owns a device operation must either abort the operation or refuse to close while it is in flight. And the working state needs a Cancel button of its own - a progress dialog with only an X, where the X does not cancel, is the shape that costs people a night.
findings.repro: Settings > Help & Tutorials > 'Capture your first light' > Start > set exposure to 999999 > Start capture > wait for 'Working on it...' > click the X in the dialog title bar > sidebar Imaging. Observe the running countdown, then click the X at the right of the image toolbar (tooltip 'Abort capture') repeatedly.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-52-working.png (progress state: no Cancel, only the title X); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-53-orphan.png ('Exposing... 999858.8s remaining' after the dialog was closed); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-54-abort.png (the 'Abort capture' tooltip visible on the highlighted X while the counter still reads 999800.7s).
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/first_light/first_light_flow_dialog.dart (no onDismiss abort, no cancel action in the running state). The dead 'Abort capture' is in the imaging viewer toolbar and does not own the first-light capture path.
findings.proposed_fix: Give the running state a Cancel button that calls the camera abort, and make the dialog's dismiss handler abort as well (or set barrierDismissible/canPop false while a capture is in flight). Separately, route the imaging viewer's abort at the camera rather than at the imaging capture controller so it can stop any in-flight exposure.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end, plus the control experiment the original finding did not run. (1) Running state has no cancel: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-13-working.png shows 'Working on it... / Capturing exposure' with an indeterminate bar and only the title-bar X; code agrees -- first_light_flow_dialog.dart:112-119, _actionsFor returns null for exposing/stretching/solving/annotating. (2) The X closes it mid-run: clicked it, dialog gone (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-15-afterx.png), no new native log lines, and Imaging still read 'Exposing... 999938.8s remaining'. (3) The Imaging 'Abort capture' X is genuinely dead for this path, not merely silent -- this is the part I proved rather than assumed. I hovered to confirm the target (tooltip beginning 'Abo', button highlighted, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-19-tooltip.png), clicked it twice; the counter ran on 999938.8 -> 999912.8 (999999 - 87.2s elapsed, recomputed) and the log gained ZERO lines. I then restarted the app, reconnected the camera, took a 120 s Snapshot FROM the Imaging screen and clicked the same X: the log immediately printed '2026-08-02T16:10:15.432291Z INFO Exposure cancelled'. So a working abort does log, and the first-light abort never reached the backend. Root cause is exactly where the finding points: imaging_screen_actions.dart:273 _abortCapture early-returns on 'if (!_isSingleCapture && !_isLooping) return;' -- imaging-screen-local flags a first-light capture never sets -- while imaging_preview_toolbar.dart:97 decides to SHOW the button from the global 'exposureProgress.remaining > 0'. The same guard means that button is offered and dead for any exposure the Imaging screen did not itself start (sequencer runs, centering); I did not drive those, so treat that as a code-level observation only. (4) Camera stayed unusable: clicking Snapshot during the orphan produced no log line and no new exposure; only killing and restarting the process cleared it. PRECISION CORRECTION for the fixer: the finding implies the modal is freely dismissible, but it is not -- first_light_flow_dialog.dart:61 wraps it in PopScope(canPop: !state.isRunning) and I verified Escape is blocked mid-run (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-14-esc.png, dialog still up). The single hole is the header close button: SkotiqDialog gates it on 'closeEnabled' (skotiq_dialog.dart:89, default true) and calls Navigator.pop directly (skotiq_dialog.dart:98-105), which PopScope does not intercept; FirstLightFlowDialog never passes closeEnabled. So the minimal fix is 'closeEnabled: !state.isRunning' plus a real cancel -- and a real cancel needs a cancel path that does not exist yet: FirstLightOrchestrator.run and firstLightControllerProvider have no cancel/abort token at all (only reset(), first_light_provider.dart:38, which clears UI state while the exposure keeps running). Severity P1 confirmed, not raised: the app-restart recovery keeps it out of P0, but a progress modal whose only exit does not cancel, backed by a device-abort button that lies, is the shape that costs a night.

findings.title: 'Resume' on the incomplete-session dialog is indistinguishable from 'Decide Later' - nothing in the UI shows the session, and it re-prompts identically on the next launch
findings.what_happened: Clicked 'Resume' on 'NGC 7000 run' (14 exposures, 1h 10m integration, status='active'). The dialog closed. Afterwards the Dashboard still read 'No run active', the top strip still read 'Idle / No Target', the status bar still read 'Idle', and 'Last run' still read 'No runs yet - your first night will appear here.' The imaging_sessions row stayed status='active'. On the next app launch the identical 'Incomplete Sessions Found' dialog reappeared for the same session with the same numbers.
findings.expected: Recovering a session should be visible: the shell/dashboard should show the adopted session (target, frames so far, integration so far) and offer a way to close it out. As built there is no surface anywhere that reflects the recovered session, so 'Resume' and 'Decide Later' have the same observable effect and the prompt recurs on every launch forever.
findings.repro: sqlite3 <scratch>/skotiq.db "insert into imaging_sessions(name,profile_id,start_time,total_exposures,successful_exposures,failed_exposures,total_integration_secs,avg_hfr,autofocus_count,status) values('NGC 7000 run',1,strftime('%s','now')-5400,20,14,1,4200.0,3.2,2,'active')" -> launch -> click Resume -> inspect the Dashboard and the DB -> relaunch.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-58-recovery3.png (the card before Resume); tree after Resume shows only 'panel: No run active' / 'panel: Last run' / 'panel: No runs yet - your first night will appear here.'; sqlite 'select id,name,status from imaging_sessions' -> '1|NGC 7000 run|active'; tree after the next launch shows 'panel: Incomplete Sessions Found' with the same 'NGC 7000 run / 14 exposures / 1h 10m total / HFR: 3.20 / 1 failed'.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/session_recovery_dialog.dart:229 (_recoverSession) -> skotiq_core session_provider.dart:228 recoverSession sets SessionState(isActive: true, ...), which no desktop surface renders.
findings.proposed_fix: Either render the recovered session (a 'Session in progress' chip in the shell status bar with an End session action), or make Resume adopt-and-close the session so it stops re-prompting. Silently setting provider state nobody displays is the worst of the three options.
findings.verdict_reasoning: The central assertion does not hold. I ran the A/B the original finding never ran. Seeded imaging_sessions id=1 'NGC 7000 run' status='active' with 14 captured_images; launched; got the identical 'Incomplete Sessions Found' card. RUN A — clicked Resume: Analytics > Session rendered header 'Current Session' / 'Started: Aug 3, 2026 15:30' with a live-ticking DURATION 01:32:22, EXPOSURES 14/0, INTEGRATION 1h 10m, MEDIAN HFR 3.20. RUN B — relaunched and clicked Decide Later: the SAME tab rendered 'Reviewing' + selector chrome and header 'NGC 7000 run' / 'Mon Aug 3, 2026 · 15:30 · active' with DURATION 0s. Different code paths: session_tab.dart:39-41 computes isLive = sessionState.isActive && sessionState.dbSessionId == reviewSessionId and only the isLive branch (:58-68) emits 'Current Session'/'Started:'. So the recovered SessionState IS rendered by a desktop surface and Resume is observably distinct from Decide Later. WHAT SURVIVES, worth refiling as its own narrower P3: the Dashboard still reads 'No run active', the top strip 'Idle / No Target', 'Last run' still 'No runs yet', and the prompt DOES recur identically on the next launch (verified by relaunching after Resume) because recovery lives only in memory.
findings.location_wrong: The cited lines are correct as far as they go (session_recovery_dialog.dart:229 _recoverSession; session_provider.dart:228 recoverSession setting SessionState(isActive: true) at :237-247), but the conclusion drawn from them — 'which no desktop surface renders' — is false: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/analytics_screen/session_tab.dart:39-68 renders exactly that state.

findings.title: The NIGHT STORY timeline (and every narrator detail sheet) is hidden whenever the session has no science products, even when narrator events exist
findings.what_happened: With session 1 holding 3 narrator_events rows and 14 captured_images rows but zero science products, Analytics > Science rendered the shared empty state ('Turn pretty pictures into real measurements / Show me the 5 steps') and the NIGHT STORY section did not exist anywhere in the widget tree - so the narrator detail sheet was unreachable. I then inserted 5 rows into transparency_samples for the same session and nothing else; on the next launch the identical session rendered 'NIGHT STORY / 3 quality notes - 2 warnings' with all three events, each of which opens the detail sheet.
findings.expected: The Night Narrator is a session-narrative surface, not a science product. A user who imaged all night without a plate solver (which is exactly the user the narrator is written for - 'Guiding RMS doubled after the meridian flip', 'Lost 22 minutes to cloud') gets no story at all. NIGHT STORY should render whenever the session has narrator events, independently of the photometry/transparency/PSF emptiness test.
findings.repro: Seed imaging_sessions + captured_images + narrator_events for one session, leave all science tables empty, open Analytics > Science with that session selected: empty on-ramp, no NIGHT STORY. Insert any row into transparency_samples for that session and relaunch: NIGHT STORY appears with the same events.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-67.png (empty on-ramp, no NIGHT STORY, same session selected, 'Plate solve health 0% - 0 of 14 solved'); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-70-story3.png (after the transparency insert: NIGHT STORY with 'Guiding RMS doubled after the meridian flip 09:44', 'Focus drifted 84 steps as the tube cooled 10:00', 'Lost 22 minutes to cloud 10:17'); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-71-narratorsheet.png (the detail sheet).
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/science_analytics_tab.dart:451-513 - the `allEmpty` test covers only science products, and its early-return branch omits the NIGHT STORY section built at :666-672.
findings.proposed_fix: Include the narrator feed in the emptiness test, or render the NIGHT STORY section inside the allEmpty branch alongside ScienceStatusBanner and ScienceSolveRateCard.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced as a controlled single-variable experiment. Session 1 seeded with 14 captured_images and 3 narrator_events and ZERO science products: Analytics > Science selected 'NGC 7000 run · Aug 3, 2026 15:30 · 14 frames', showed 'Plate solve health / 0 of 14 solved' and the shared empty on-ramp 'Turn pretty pictures into real measurements / Show me the 5 steps', and the tree contained no NIGHT STORY node anywhere. I then inserted 5 rows into transparency_samples for the same session and changed nothing else; on relaunch the identical session rendered 'NIGHT STORY / 1 milestone · 3 quality notes · 2 warnings' with all three events as tappable buttons. Source confirms the allEmpty predicate tests only science products and never narrator events.
findings.location_wrong: Line numbers have drifted ~20 lines. In the current tree the allEmpty predicate is at science_analytics_tab.dart:473-483 (not :451-513), its early-return branch is :488-536, and the NIGHT STORY heading + NightStoryTimeline(sessionId: activeSessionId) is at :687-693 (not :666-672). File and mechanism are correct.

findings.title: Pinning a narrator event is invisible on the timeline - the PINNED marker only exists inside the detail sheet
findings.what_happened: Event 2 was stored with pinned=1. On the NIGHT STORY timeline its row is visually identical to the two unpinned rows - same dot, same layout, no pin glyph, no ordering change. The 'PINNED' label appears only after you open that specific event's detail sheet.
findings.expected: Pinning exists so an operator can mark the two or three things that mattered in an eight-hour night. A pin you can only see by opening each item one at a time is not a pin. Show a pin glyph on the timeline row (and ideally offer a 'Pinned only' chip next to the existing All/Discoveries/Milestones/Conditions/Equipment/Quality filters).
findings.repro: Set pinned=1 on one narrator_events row, open Analytics > Science > NIGHT STORY, compare the three rows, then open each one.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-70-story3.png (three visually identical rows); tree after tapping the middle row: 'panel: PINNED' / 'panel: Focus drifted 84 steps as the tube cooled'.

findings.title: Dashboard Glance-mode toggle reports itself as DISABLED to assistive tech while working normally
findings.what_happened: The accessibility tree reports 'button: Glance mode [off,DISABLED]'. Clicking it works - the same node then reads '[ON,DISABLED]' - so the control is live but permanently advertises itself as unavailable. Its Semantics wrapper sets button: true and toggled: enabled but never sets enabled: true, so the node never carries the ENABLED flag.
findings.expected: A working toggle must announce as enabled. As built a screen-reader user is told the dashboard's Glance-mode control is dimmed and will skip it.
findings.repro: Dashboard -> `drive_linux.py tree --profile r-shared-widgets | grep -i glance` -> click the eye icon in the dashboard header strip -> tree again.
findings.evidence: tree before: 'button: Glance mode [off,DISABLED]'; after one click: 'button: Glance mode [ON,DISABLED]'. Same dumps carry correctly-enabled buttons such as 'button: Connect equipment' with no DISABLED flag, so the harness does read the flag when it is published.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/glance_mode_toggle.dart:60-64 (Semantics(button: true, toggled: enabled, label: 'Glance mode') - no `enabled:`); found while auditing its TouchTargetFloor wrapper at :73.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `enabled: !_saving` to that Semantics node. This is the same omission as the guide-controls finding above; a lint or a shared toggle widget would catch the class.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Live tree on the rebuilt bundle: 'button: Glance mode [off,DISABLED]'; one click and the same node reads 'button: Glance mode [ON,DISABLED]' — the control works but permanently advertises itself as unavailable. Source at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/glance_mode_toggle.dart:60-63 is Semantics(button: true, toggled: enabled, label: 'Glance mode') with no `enabled:` property, so the node publishes CHECKABLE but never ENABLED/SENSITIVE. Location correct, including the note that it was found via the TouchTargetFloor wrapper at :73.

findings.title: Four widgets are exported from the app barrel but have zero call sites - dead UI shipping in the binary
findings.what_happened: Repo-wide search (packages/ + apps/, excluding each widget's own file) finds no instantiation of ObjectInfoPanel (0 references anywhere, including tests), TourSelectionSheet (0 references to TourSelectionSheet.show), SequenceControls (referenced only by test/widgets/run_controls_paused_skip_test.dart) or VariablePickerField/VariablePickerButton (VariablePickerButton appears only as the suffixIcon of VariablePickerField in the same file; VariablePickerField has no callers outside test/widgets/variable_picker_test.dart). All four are nonetheless exported from packages/skotiq_app/lib/skotiq_app.dart (lines 37, 39, 46, and the sequence barrel).
findings.expected: Either wire them up or delete them. Two of them carry doc comments that assert they are in use and are therefore actively misleading: tour_selection_sheet.dart:7-8 says 'Used from Settings and contextual prompts' (Settings > Help & Tutorials builds its own inline 'Tutorial Tours' list and never calls it) and variable_picker.dart advertises a picker no sequencer field offers - Settings > Sequencer only mentions it in a comment. A sequencer that stores ${TARGET}/${FILTER}-style variables but exposes no picker is a real capability gap, not just dead code.
findings.repro: grep -rn 'ObjectInfoPanel|TourSelectionSheet|SequenceControls|VariablePickerField' --include='*.dart' packages apps, excluding each widget's own file. Also confirmed live: the Sequencer and Settings > Sequencer screens have no variable-insert control, and Settings > Help & Tutorials has no tour bottom sheet (its Tutorial Tours rows are inline list tiles).
findings.evidence: source-only for the zero-reference claim (a widget with no call site cannot be observed in the running app, which IS the finding); the live half - that Settings > Help & Tutorials renders its own inline tour list rather than the sheet - is in /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-50-help.png.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/object_info_panel.dart, widgets/tour_selection_sheet.dart, widgets/sequence_controls.dart, widgets/sequence/variable_picker.dart; barrel exports in packages/skotiq_app/lib/skotiq_app.dart:37,39,46.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete object_info_panel.dart and sequence_controls.dart (both superseded - the planetarium's object_details_panel and the sequencer's own run controls). For variable_picker, wire VariablePickerField into the sequencer's filename/target text fields, which is what it was written for. For tour_selection_sheet, either call it from Settings > Help & Tutorials or drop it and fix the doc comment.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Verified by exhaustive repo search on the current tree. ObjectInfoPanel: ZERO references anywhere in packages/ or apps/ outside its own file, including tests. TourSelectionSheet: ZERO references anywhere, including contextual_tour_prompt.dart, while its own doc at tour_selection_sheet.dart:7-8 asserts 'Used from Settings and contextual prompts' — Settings > Help & Tutorials builds its own inline list at help_tutorials_settings.dart:159. SequenceControls: only doc-comment mentions in mobile_sequence_overlay.dart:14,16 plus test/widgets/run_controls_paused_skip_test.dart:123. VariablePickerField/VariablePickerButton: only test/widgets/variable_picker_test.dart. Downgraded P3->P4: no user-visible misbehaviour; the dead-code half is hygiene and the one user-facing observation (the sequencer interpolates ${TARGET}/${FILTER} but offers no insert control) is a missing feature, not a defect.
findings.location_wrong: One factual error inside the claim: variable_picker.dart is NOT exported from any barrel. There is no 'sequence barrel' export for it in packages/skotiq_app/lib/skotiq_app.dart; the only import anywhere is the direct path import in test/widgets/variable_picker_test.dart:7. So three of the four are barrel-exported dead code and the fourth is unexported dead code. The three cited line numbers (37, 39, 46) are exact.
